questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was interested in going to Italy to also try and learn some Italian.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy, however always a bit confusing to learn a new university system.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had some mails from UNIMI's Erasmus office, but maybe there could have been an introduction meeting where you could also get to meet some other erasmus students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I used quite some time on it before. I just used a site, where the site had confirmed the accommodation beforehand, so I knew it wasn't a scam. However it made it a bit more expensive. I used Uniplaces.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Milan is quite expensive.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't know so much about it.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You just changed the study plan on the university website and then followed the courses. The real binding registration only happened, when you registered for the exam. This made it more flexible if you wanted to change courses, which I liked.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could write to different university mail's and also there was several international welcome desk on campus, where you could drop by for questions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try some different courses out the first week of classes, to make sure you end up following a course you like.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think it carried a lot. Sometimes I felt it was a bit below UCPH when it came to writing texts and analysing, but there was more focus on testing the students knowledge of the readings, so sometimes I think it was more demanding in terms of exams.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More focused on memorisation at UNIMI.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
ETHICAL THEORY AND HARD CHOICES
POLITICAL ORDER, VIOLENCE AND INSTITUTIONS
GLOBAL CHALLENGES TO DEMOCRACY
CRITICAL THINKING AND ARGUMENTATION
AMERICAN HISTORY AND POLITICS

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
AMERICAN HISTORY AND POLITICS (was quite fun subject and interesting material)
ETHICAL THEORY AND HARD CHOICES (a little demanding in terms of exams, but if you have the time, I think it was also quite interesting)
CRITICAL THINKING AND ARGUMENTATION (fun little course, and very different style)

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I can't remember any.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Coffee (cheap), housing (expensive)
Oats (more expensive than Copenhagen)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't really seek it out, so don't know.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were some athletic activities I know, but I don't think there was enough of social activities, where you met other students.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Hiking around the city in the mountains.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Again hiking around the city in the mountains. Going to the lakes up north. Just walk around Milan.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy and interesting I think.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I just talked to the people in the classes I took, which was really nice and interesting, so it wasn't only erasmus students you get to meet.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I can't remember any.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really like the culture in general and it was just a fresh new thing compared to Denmark.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Remember to;
- Explore things around Milan (lakes, cities, mountains)
- Use the flexible course registration to try out the courses in the first week before settling on some
- Be in good time with accommodation

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I don't know.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Living in Italy, learning some of the language, meeting new people, and challenging myself in a different academic setting.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Some of the exams.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
